title: Good decision: StateChange type defined in kith-core, not kith-events
description:
Decision: StateChange is defined in kith-core/src/events.rs. kith-events re-exports it. Store crates and handler both import from kith-core.

Code location: kith-core/src/events.rs (lines 10-16), kith-events/src/lib.rs (line 3 re-export).

Why this is correct: Avoids circular dependencies. StateChange is emitted by the store layer (kith-store), so store crates must import it. If StateChange were defined in kith-events, then kith-store would depend on kith-events. But kith-events depends on kith-core and uses kith-store in its tests. Placing StateChange in the shared type layer (kith-core) breaks the cycle: store crates import from kith-core (already their dep), and kith-events imports from kith-core without creating a reverse dep on store.

The wrong alternative would be to define StateChange in kith-events. This creates a circular import: kith-store → kith-events → kith-core, but kith-events also imports kith-store for testing (test_store_set_events_tx), forming a cycle.

This is proper layering: common types at the bottom, specialized types only where they're needed.
